reported_success.location: pp. 10–11, Social Distance: Self-Other Asymmetry in Total Trait Ascriptions
reported_success.quote: We found support for the hypothesis that trait ascriptions would differ based on social distance

notes: Requested printed test statistics retained as effect values. Replication also prints Cohen’s f = 0.10, 95% CI [0.04, 0.17]. Authors describe the target replication signal as inconsistent with the original because its magnitude was smaller (pp. 10–11); the successful label records their explicit support for the social-distance hypothesis, not a significance-based inference. Their paper-wide verdict is mixed, which covers other hypotheses. Replication p. 10 pools temporal conditions in a combined design, whereas the original target contrast concerns current assessments; target_match is therefore false for the located replication test. Original analytic n is null: only the all-condition undergraduate n is printed, and no sample size was derived from degrees of freedom. Quotes preserve PDF text extraction glyphs; whitespace has been normalized. Both cached full texts were retrieved through public author-hosted links and titles verified.
